//: Allowlist of retained IronPulse identifiers. Each entry pins a file glob to the exact substrings that may appear there and the compatibility reason. The brand-audit script rejects any ironpulse occurrence not covered here, and rejects any mettlelift occurrence anywhere.

compatibility.reason: iOS/Android bundle identifier — cannot change without breaking existing installs on Apple and Google stores. EAS project slug is also fixed at `ironpulse` for the same reason.
IAP product identifiers registered with App Store Connect and Google Play — renaming would create a new SKU and lose subscribers.
Client PowerSync SQLite filename — renaming would orphan existing offline data on every device.
Postgres role, password, and database name — changing these requires a coordinated dump/restore migration across every self-hosted instance and every CI job.
MinIO/S3 bucket name — changing would require object migration and would break existing signed URLs.
Docker container and service names — renaming would break existing docker-compose volumes and named networks on running deployments.
Backup filename convention — restore.sh, backup.sh, and verify-backup.sh all look for ironpulse_*.sql.gz; existing backups must remain restorable.
Legacy deep-link scheme — retained as alias so notification URLs, share links, and OAuth callbacks issued before the rebrand keep resolving.
Developer hostname alias — kept so existing engineer /etc/hosts entries, Caddyfile blocks, and cached OAuth callback registrations still work.
Forgejo and GitHub repository paths remain at hiten/IronPulse per TASK-21 compatibility decision.

Historical context in specs, plans, ADRs, and the changelog — these are frozen records of past decisions and must retain the names in use at the time. The audit skips these paths entirely rather than allowlisting individual strings.
Self-hosting documentation refers to the primary web container by its retained service name.
Nightly Maestro script pins the workspace path to the retained IronPulse checkout.
